The drug is directly targeting Ectonucleotide pyrophosphatase/phosphodiesterase family member 6, which in turn is a target of 9-Isovaleroxy Balanophonin. This suggests a potential pathway where Ligelizumab may modulate the activity of the Ectonucleotide pyrophosphatase/phosphodiesterase family member 6, which could influence the function of Solute carrier organic anion transporter family member 1B1. The evidence implies that Ligelizumab may act as a modulator of the transporter, potentially affecting the transport of organic anions, which is a key function of this family member. The integration of these targets highlights a possible role for Ligelizumab in regulating the activity of the transporter, though the exact mechanism of interaction remains to be fully elucidated.
